sections.brief: Absolute mobility 92% (1940 cohort) to 50% (1980, 1984; Chetty et al. Science 2017): method (CPS + Census + 1980-82 tax copula, CPI-U-RS, age 30, pre-tax family income), by parent percentile (94/93/88 vs 70/45/33), sons 95 to 41, states (Michigan -48); counterfactuals 62% growth vs 80% shared growth (not a top-1% decomposition); robustness; Winship (60/67/68%, three in four) and Strain (nearly three-quarters); where it holds (bottom 10th pct 70%); no post-1984 cohort estimate as of Oct 2026; labelled interpretation (Sophia illusion thesis) with counter-readings. Figures: stats; money; compare (told vs record)

Relative mobility stable (rank-rank ~0.30, 1971-82 cohorts; bottom-to-top 8.4% to 9.0%; college gap 74.5 to 69.2; 'birth lottery' larger); geography (7.5% national, Charlotte 4.4, SLC 10.8, San Jose 12.9; five correlates); causal evidence (exposure 4%/yr, MTO +31% before 13 only); Opportunity Atlas (2018; AER 2026; 1984-89 data 2024); economic connectedness (Nature 2022, ~20%); race (99% of tracts; Changing Opportunity -30% low-income race gap, +30% class gap); designed vs captured friction pointers; where it works. Figures: stats; flow; compare (told vs record)

IGE and the Great Gatsby curve (Corak 2013; Krueger 12 Jan 2012; US 0.47, Canada 0.19, Denmark 0.15); Canada-US differences at the extremes; OECD 2018 (4-5 generations average, US 5, Denmark 2, internal Nordic inconsistency, sticky ceilings); absolute mobility abroad (Manduca et al. 2020: US/Canada ~50%, Norway ~75%, Denmark 50% pre-tax/65%+ post-tax; US income 71% of GDP growth vs Norway 95%); Berman (US fall 39.2 pts, 24.6 inequality); critics (Landerso-Heckman, Kirkegaard, Winship on IGE); where it works. Figures: stats; compare (levels and drivers); compare (told vs record)
